name: Straatsma Syndrome
aliases: Myelinated Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer with Amblyopia and Myopia

criteria.description: Presence of extensive myelinated retinal nerve fiber layer visible on fundoscopic examination
High myopia typically greater than -6.00 diopters
Unilateral amblyopia associated with the affected eye
Possible optic disc anomalies such as tilted disc or peripapillary atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: myelinated retinal nerve fibers, high myopia, and amblyopia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical based on ophthalmological examination; imaging and refraction tests support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extensive myelinated retinal nerve fiber layer
pathognomonic.notes: Visible as white, feathery patches on fundus examination
searchTerms: excess myelin in eye nerve layer

pathognomonic.notes: Reduced visual acuity in the affected eye

common.notes: Misalignment of the eyes often associated with amblyopia
Atrophy around the optic nerve head

occasional.notes: Involuntary eye movements in some cases
Irregular curvature of the cornea or lens

rare.notes: Underdevelopment of the optic nerve in rare cases
Rare complication due to high myopia

imaging: Fundoscopic examination showing myelinated retinal nerve fibers
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating retinal nerve fiber layer abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered sporadic
other: Visual acuity testing showing unilateral amblyopia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of myelinated retinal nerve fibers without associated amblyopia or high myopia
Underdeveloped optic nerve with visual impairment but absence of myelinated retinal nerve fibers
High myopia present without myelinated retinal nerve fibers or amblyopia

references: Straatsma BR, Heckenlively JR, Foos RY, Taylor GN. Myelinated retinal nerve fibers, amblyopia, and myopia: a syndrome. Arch Ophthalmol. 1979;97(11):2057-2061.
American Academy of Ophthalmology. Myelinated Retinal Nerve Fibers. Ophthalmology Reference.
